routes.name: Short Term Employment Permit with Work Permit and leave to remain
Long Term Employment Permit with Work Permit and leave to remain

note: Guernsey (the Bailiwick: Guernsey, Alderney, Sark and Herm), read on the States of Guernsey's immigration page and its fee list in force from 1 September 2026, and its Employment Permit Policy FAQ (gov.gg), on 2026-10-30. Anyone not a British or Irish citizen needs permission to take employment: since 3 April 2023 one Employment Permit under the Population Management Law (a Short Term STEP, a Seasonal SEP or a Long Term LTEP) carries the immigration work permit, a work visa or further leave to remain following it; EU/EEA/Swiss nationals arriving now need a visa like anyone else. A STEP is issued for up to 12 months, renewable, until three consecutive years' residence; with the work permit for up to a year (£100) and 12 months' leave to remain as a work permit holder (£300) it is kept as £400 for 12 months. An LTEP's work permit for up to three years (£300) and leave to remain beyond 12 months (£943) are kept together as £1,243 for three years. The permits are for the job and employer (work for the sponsor); the visa is applied for from abroad and further leave in the island (either). Indefinite leave to remain costs £3,226; the years it asks aren't on the pages read, so none are kept. British and Irish citizens need no immigration permission but do need an Employment Permit to live in local market housing, which the form doesn't hold as a route. Naturalisation costs £1,709 (not held here).

Work permit including any variation / change of employment - valid for up to 3 years £300 ... Leave to remain for 12 months as a work permit holder £300 ... Leave to remain longer than 12 months as a work permit holder (LTEP only) £943 ... Indefinite leave to remain £3226

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Employment Permit Policy FAQ
sources.said: Short Term Employment Permits will continue to be issued for up to 12 months, renewable upon expiry. However, the holder will now only be able to hold a STEP until they reach a total of 3 consecutive years of residence in Guernsey. ... in order for a person to be granted a work visa or Further Leave to Remain (for employment purposes), they will be required to hold a STEP, SEP or LTEP. ... any new EU/EEA/Swiss nationals now need to apply for a visa to live and work in Guernsey.
